newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-CIGAR-PUFFING GAZZA REVELS IN RANGERS' DOMINANCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-CIGAR-PUFFING GAZZA REVELS IN RANGERS' DOMINANCE.

text.p: One moment above all others in Glasgow Rangers' weekend demolition of Heart of Midlothian summed up the Scottish champions' near-invincibility this season. Inevitably, it involved Paul Gascoigne.

With Rangers' well on their way to a 4-1 victory which took them 14 points clear of nearest premier division rivals Celtic, the England midfielder bamboozled his marker and released a perfect pass before being bundled to the ground by a clumsy late tackle.
As play continued Gazza sat on the Tyncastle pitch with his fingers to his lips puffing on an imaginary cigar. It was all so easy.

The extent to which Rangers dominated Saturday's match raises more questions about the health of a league which Walter Smith's side look set to conquer for a record-equalling ninth time in a row and 47th time in all.
Given that Celtic have won the championship a further 35 times, chalking up their own nine-in-a-row between 1966-74, there is precious little space for any team outside Glasgow on the honours board.

Once again the title-race has been reduced to a single-city affair by Christmas and if Rangers beat Celtic in the old firm clash on January 2 the contest between Scotland's two giants will be all but over too.
It all makes for a fairly dull spring in which the scrap to avoid relegation from Scotland's miniature 10-team top flight is more exciting than the battle to conquer it.
The other side of the coin is the performance of Scottish sides in Europe, where Rangers, a permanent presence in the Champions' League in recent years, have won only once since March 1993.
The quality of opposition at home hardly prepares the Scottish champions for clashes against the likes of Ajax and Juventus, both of whom strolled away from Ibrox with victories.

Hearts pointed to the first-half sending off of Neil Pointon as the turning point in Saturday's match but, in truth, rarely can a dismissal have been so irrelevant. Rangers looked to have several extra man on the pitch from the start.
So, a fixture which promised to rattle Rangers ultimately proved to be little more than a simple Hearts by-pass operation for the champions on the road towards title number 47.
No-one can doubt their determination -- the club has even cancelled their Christmas party so as to concentrate minds ahead of the Celtic clash.
"For the time being, parties will have to come second and families will have to be forgotten about," defender Alan McClaren said solemnly on Saturday. "We can always have a big party in May."
One current form, and against current opposition, few would bet against that.
